applies_why: The judge text resolves the D6/C4 collision between descent according to the flesh and conception of the Holy Ghost, which is the chain-versus-chain weighing Rule K-C governs.
quote: D6 vs C4 (Romans 1:3): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] section A.1-2 and [CR3] Link 6 premises 1-3, where descent according to the flesh is weighed against conception of the Holy Ghost without explicit textual resolution of paternity.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: Phrase: that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires. Reading one: this forbids deciding by lack of an explicit contrary or resolving verse and requires chain-by-footing; reading two: a judge may still call a collision underdetermined merely because no verse explicitly resolves paternity.
why: Because it makes lack of explicit textual resolution of paternity decisive, the judge applies the retired stating-verse test rather than weighing the chains by footing alone.
